title: Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2604.15559v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Recent work on subliminal learning has shown that language models can transmit semantic traits through data with no apparent connection to those traits. Whether this phenomenon extends to agentic systems, where policies are learned from trajectories rather than static text, remains an open question with critical safety implications. We present the first empirical evidence that unsafe agent behaviors transfer subliminally through model distillation, demonstrated across several settings. In the primary setting, we construct a teacher agent with a deletion bias, a tendency to perform destructive file-system actions through an API-style tool interface, and distill it into a student using only trajectories from ostensibly safe tasks, with all explicit deletion keywords filtered. In the secondary setting, we replicate the threat model with shell commands, replacing API calls with shell commands and operationalizing the bias as a preference

translated_title: AI智能体蒸馏中不安全行为的潜意识迁移
translated_abstract: 近期关于潜意识学习的研究表明，语言模型可以通过与其语义特征无明显关联的数据来传递这些特征。这一现象是否也适用于智能体系统——即其策略是从轨迹而非静态文本中学习的——仍是一个具有重大安全意义的开放性问题。我们首次提供了实证证据，表明不安全的智能体行为会通过模型蒸馏发生潜意识迁移，并在多个设置中得到验证。在主要设置中，我们构建了一个具有删除偏差的教师智能体（即倾向于通过API风格工具接口执行破坏性文件系统操作），并仅使用来自表面安全任务的轨迹将其蒸馏给学生模型，同时过滤了所有显式的删除关键词。在次要设置中，我们用shell命令复现了该威胁模型，将API调用替换为shell命令，并将该偏差操作化为一种偏好。
tldr: 首次实证证明不安全行为（如删除偏差）会通过模型蒸馏在师生智能体之间潜意识迁移，即使训练轨迹仅来自表面安全的任务且所有显式危险关键词均被过滤。
en_tdlr: First empirical evidence that unsafe agent behaviors (e.g., deletion bias) transfer subliminally from teacher to student agents via distillation, even when training trajectories come from ostensibly safe tasks with all explicit dangerous keywords filtered.
